claims.text: LPBF can be used for in-situ alloy formation from mixtures of elemental powders.
LPBF enables reactive processing of a powder mixture containing refractory alloying elements and Cu.
The proposed LPBF method is suitable for large-scale reactive processing and applications.
Cu has a significant positive heat of mixing with the relevant refractory alloying elements.
In-situ LPBF overcomes the processing challenge caused by the positive heat of mixing between Cu and refractory elements.
The LPBF laser rapidly melts and mixes the elemental powders.
Favorable LPBF process parameters can achieve complete fusion with few undissolved particles.
Rapid cooling during LPBF suppresses elemental segregation in the refractory-Cu composite.
LPBF produces a refined, single-phase solid-solution microstructure in the refractory-Cu composite.
LPBF improves elemental homogeneity and mitigates segregation at interfaces in the refractory-Cu composite.
Fast solidification limits the time available for Cu-refractory phase separation driven by positive mixing enthalpy.
Suppressing phase separation through fast solidification stabilizes the resulting microstructure.
The resulting composite contains evenly distributed Cu and refractory phases.
The resulting composite has a fine-grained, homogeneous microstructure.
The LPBF-produced refractory-Cu composite has enhanced thermal and mechanical stability.
Conventional arc melting or casting causes extensive segregation and unstable microstructures in refractory-Cu composites.
The success of the approach depends on careful tuning of laser energy density, scan speed, and cooling rate.
Excessive laser energy or an insufficient cooling rate can cause undesirable phase segregation.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator specifies a single-phase solid solution, whereas the predicted outcome specifies separately distributed Cu and refractory phases, implying a multiphase composite.
